messages:
Aisha: Heads-up — deploy window tonight for model-routing service. Change window 01:30-03:30 UTC. High-level: deploy v3.1.0, hold pin to v3.0.7 for canary users, then soft-enable flag `model_route_v3` with a staggered ramp. Will validate perf and roll-forward afterwards. @deploy-bot schedule at 01:30 pls.

deploy-bot: scheduled deployment job at 01:30 UTC. Canary schedule: global 0.5% -> 2% -> 8% over 25m. EU cohort uses conservative ramp: 0.5 -> 1 -> 2 -> 5 -> 8 with 5m waits. Auto-rollback thresholds: errors >2.5% OR p99 > 2.5x baseline for 2 consecutive samples. Owners: Aisha (release lead), Ravi (ops), Tom (platform).

Ravi: added short checklist to release notes. Quick clarification: do we want an explicit fallback pin in the service manifest or rely on toggle only?

Aisha: add both. Fallback pin in service metadata makes fallback faster if we need a full pin reversion. Toggle off is immediate but pinning helps routing consistency. Use fallback v3.0.6.

Tom: I'll attach a small script to the deploy docs that can force the pin and annotate the incident: `./admin pin-service model-routing v3.0.6 --reason "rollback from v3.1.0"` — requires admin token.

Lena: Note on observability: enable synthetic probes against the canary cohort + full-traffic perf probes. Also enable the cost delta monitor for token spend; new model path increases per-token work.

deploy-bot: Canary started at 01:30 UTC. EU using conservative schedule. Monitoring hooks: perf-dash, synth-probes, error-alerts, billing-delta.

Ravi: watching errors and latency. So far stable at first two windows. No error spike.

deploy-bot: Canary update: global bumped to 2% at +7m; EU progressed to 1% at +7m. No triggers.

Lena: seeing a slight uptick in tail latency for long sequences in eu-central (~30% higher p99 for >512 tokens). It's not over alert threshold but we should slow EU ramp by 10m.

Aisha: agreed. Tom, hold EU progression by 10m. Everyone okay with that?

Tom: holding EU ramp. Made note in release thread.

deploy-bot: EU hold applied. Global remains on schedule.

Ravi: small error surge in a backend pool (auth proxy) coincident with EU ramp attempt — investigating if unrelated. If errors cross 2.5% we trigger auto-rollback.

Lena: auth proxy issue looks like a connection pool saturation — mitigation deployed, metrics stabilizing. No rollback.

deploy-bot: Global moved to 8% at +25m. EU finished conservative ramp to 8% after extra holds. No auto-rollback. Canary complete. Scheduled cleanup: unpin window at 04:00 UTC.

Aisha: post-canary actions: - validate evaluation suite against the top 200 prompts - check cost delta for first 2 hours - confirm no SLO regressions in next 1h before unpin. Ravi on first hour, Tom on second hour.

Ravi: I'll own 0-1h monitoring and will escalate if I see sustained p99 > 1.8x baseline or errors >1.5%.

Tom: I'll run the unpin at 04:00 if green and update the changelog. Script to unpin: `./admin unpin-service model-routing v3.1.0 --confirm`.

Lena: leaving a note: remember to add the reason in changelog why we used a temporary pin (routing instability during ramp). Helps audit.

Aisha: thanks all. If any manual rollback needed, steps: 1) `/ff toggle model_route_v3 off --immediate` 2) run admin pin to fallback v3.0.6 3) create incident and assign page.

Tom: acknowledged.

deploy-bot: Cleanup job scheduled: unpin at 04:00 UTC, will send final status.

Aisha: closing thread — nice job. Ping here if anything urgent. :rocket:
